claims.text: Well drilling is the process of creating a subterranean hole to reach groundwater or geological formations.
claims.label: the purpose of the borehole

claims.text: Drilling begins with geological surveys, using techniques such as seismic refraction and geophysical logging, to map the subsurface strata and choose the best location for the well.
claims.label: the geological survey

claims.text: A drilling rig is brought to the site, carrying a rotating drill bit, a powerful engine and a system for managing drilling fluids.
claims.label: the drilling rig

claims.text: Drilling fluids known as mud are pumped down the borehole to lubricate and cool the bit, carry cuttings out, and stabilize the walls of the hole against collapse.
claims.label: the role of drilling mud

claims.text: Casing, a sturdy steel pipe, is inserted into the borehole to give it structural integrity, keep the groundwater from being contaminated, and allow a pump to be installed.
claims.label: the steel casing

claims.text: The depth of the well is set by the desired yield, the geological conditions and local regulations.
claims.label: what sets the well depth

claims.text: A pump is placed at the top of the finished well to draw water up to the surface.
claims.label: the surface pump
